projectBackground.name: Founder Accelerator — HomeMeal Subscription
projectBackground.context: HomeMeal sells weekly meal boxes. Growth is strong but cash is draining. Investors will ask about unit economics and runway.

manager.name: Daniel Okoye
manager.note: Investors fund evidence, not enthusiasm. Know your payback, your churn and how many months of cash you have left.

assignment.title: Prepare the startup for investors
assignment.brief: Calculate payback, lifetime value and runway, choose the right MVP experiment and write a pitch.

documents.name: Unit Economics
documents.note: CAC €120; ARPU €30 per month; gross margin 80%; monthly churn 5%.

documents.name: Customer Interviews
documents.note: Seven of ten customers say they would be 'very disappointed' without the product.

tasks.title: CAC Payback
tasks.prompt: CAC is €120, ARPU €30 per month and gross margin 80%. What is the payback period in months?
tasks.reasoning: Payback tells you how long cash is tied up in acquiring a customer.
tasks.mistake: Using revenue gives 4 months, which is too optimistic.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Customer Lifetime Value
tasks.prompt: Monthly churn is 5% (lifetime 20 months). With ARPU €30 and 80% margin, what is LTV (€)?
tasks.tip: A healthy LTV/CAC is often 3 or more.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Runway
tasks.prompt: Cash is €240,000 and net burn is €30,000 per month. What is the runway in months?
tasks.reasoning: Runway sets the time to prove the next milestone.
tasks.tip: Plan fundraising at 6+ months of runway.
tasks.mistake: Waiting until 2 months left removes negotiating power.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: MVP
tasks.prompt: What is the best use of an MVP?
options: Test the riskiest assumption with real customers as cheaply as possible
tasks.reasoning: An MVP exists to learn fast.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Product-Market Fit Signals
options: Strong retention after the first months
Customers say they'd be very disappointed without it
Many sign-ups with no repeat use
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Investor Pitch
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence pitch covering problem, traction and the ask.
tasks.modelAnswer: Busy professionals waste hours each week deciding what to cook and shopping for it. HomeMeal delivers weekly meal boxes with a 5-month CAC payback and an LTV/CAC of 4, and seven in ten customers say they would be very disappointed without us. We are raising €500,000 to extend runway from 8 to 24 months and expand into two new cities. The main risk is churn; our retention programme targets 4% monthly.
tasks.reasoning: A good pitch states the problem, proof, ask and the main risk.
tasks.mistake: Enthusiasm without numbers does not raise money.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Startup That Ran Out of Road
caseStudy.background: A start-up grew fast but never calculated runway. When the next round failed it had six weeks of cash and had to lay off half the team.
caseStudy.challenges: Growth was prioritised over unit economics.
questions: How do you balance growth and cash?
caseStudy.solution: Summit coached founders to track runway monthly and begin fundraising at nine months.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Know your runway; it is your clock.
